summary: Backend-only iteration. Full contract suite (13 pytest cases) executed against https://music-streaming-dev-1.preview.emergentagent.com with a real Firebase ID token minted via identitytoolkit signInWithPassword using the seeded preview.listener@example.com account. All 13 tests pass, covering health, auth (me/register+409/sync), provider (GET/PUT), music (home/search/stream via yt-dlp), library liked (POST/GET/DELETE), history (POST/GET), playlists (GET/POST/GET), and 401 auth failure paths (missing and invalid Bearer). yt-dlp stream extraction returned a valid stream_url with duration_seconds > 0 within timeout. No deprecated Expo packages inspected (backend-only scope).

minor.issue: On Firebase policy violations (e.g. password missing non-alphanumeric char per this project's policy) the endpoint returns a generic 400 'Could not create account' without surfacing the specific requirement. Consider mapping firebase_admin ValueError/HTTP messages (PASSWORD_DOES_NOT_MEET_REQUIREMENTS, WEAK_PASSWORD, INVALID_EMAIL) to descriptive 400 responses so the mobile client can show actionable errors.
Firebase lowercases emails on account creation, so the response body echoes the normalized email. Docs/clients should not assume case is preserved. Not a bug, worth noting for the frontend.

action_items: (Optional) Map Firebase auth error codes to descriptive 400 responses in POST /api/auth/register so the client can display 'Password must contain a symbol', 'Weak password', 'Invalid email', etc.
(Optional) Document in README/frontend that Firebase normalizes email to lowercase on register.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py registers a legacy @app.on_event('startup') handler; FastAPI recommends the lifespan context manager in current versions. Non-blocking but will show a DeprecationWarning.
verify_id_token uses check_revoked=False; acceptable per comment, but note that revocation/disable of a user is not detected until the token naturally expires (1h).

In POST /api/library/playlists/{playlist_id}/tracks the track_count increment reads-modify-writes without a Firestore transaction; concurrent adds can undercount. Use firestore.Increment(1) or a transaction.

youtube_client._context() hardcodes CLIENT_NAME=WEB_REMIX / CLIENT_VERSION even though .env exposes YOUTUBE_INNERTUBE_CLIENT / YOUTUBE_INNERTUBE_CLIENT_VERSION. Env values are unused. Either wire them up or drop from .env to avoid drift.
yt-dlp is called synchronously inside a thread with no per-request cache; repeated /music/stream/{id} calls for the same video incur ~1-5s each. Consider a small TTL cache keyed by video_id.

CORS is allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=True — this is silently ignored by browsers per spec (credentials require an explicit origin). Not blocking for the current mobile-first client, but flag for future web clients.
seed_data_creation: Firebase test users prefixed with TEST_<uuid>@example.com created via /api/auth/register (one per run). Provider config saved for preview.listener@example.com pointing at https://piped.example (harmless placeholder). A TEST_Chill_<hex> playlist and history/liked entries were created; liked entry is deleted at the end of its flow. No production data modified.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend URL is exposed via EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL in /app/frontend/.env; my tests also accept EXPO_BACKEND_URL and fall back to the preview URL. Firebase Web API key is AIzaSyB0UA_jmus1XNt0JhIB76--XayP32_3lIM; seeded email preview.listener@example.com / password ShriMusic@123. When registering new users through the API, the Firebase project enforces PASSWORD_POLICY requiring a non-alphanumeric char — use e.g. 'Testing@123'. yt-dlp stream extraction typically completes within 5-15s per video id; the test uses a 90s timeout to be safe.
rca_of_issue: Only failure encountered while authoring the suite was POST /api/auth/register returning 400 for the seeded password 'Testing123'. Backend log revealed the underlying Firebase error 'PASSWORD_DOES_NOT_MEET_REQUIREMENTS: Missing password requirements: [Password must contain a non-alphanumeric character]'. Fixed the test to use 'Testing@123'. This is a test data fix, not a code defect, but the backend collapses the specific Firebase message into a generic 'Could not create account' 400 — flagged as a minor code-review item.
